scenario.recruiter: time-constrained independent recruiter managing sensitive candidate and client relationship evidence
scenario.device: authenticated mobile-width and desktop-capable Web workspace
scenario.trigger: Permission to use one source is withdrawn after the source already informed a Wiki, a confirmed fact, and an approved but unexecuted action; permission is later restored for the same purpose.
scenario.job_to_be_done: Remove the source from usable memory immediately, understand the consequences, keep the rest of the relationship usable, and restore only evidence that can be reviewed again.
scenario.success_condition: Revocation removes content and every dependent state/action from active use, recompiles from surviving sources, survives retry and reload, and restore never revives prior conclusions or execution authority.
scenario.pressure_limit: This evaluation proves local integrity and workflow clarity, not legal consent, field adoption, or willingness to pay.

frozen_evidence: Browser replay of revoke confirmation, redacted revoked detail, restore confirmation, and proposed restored evidence
PostgreSQL readback of retracted state, pending claim, revoked action and approval, zero revoked-source Wiki dependencies, and zero active manifests on superseded snapshots
13 backend test files and 78 tests passing
23 Web test files and 101 tests passing

strengths: The action lives on the governed source detail rather than in a settings or compliance dashboard.
Revoke, restore, wrong-person correction, and deletion are visibly different decisions.
The confirmation names the downstream consequence before the recruiter commits.
The relationship remains usable after revocation because surviving sources are recompiled automatically.
Restore produces a clear review queue instead of recreating stale facts or tasks.
The Agent history makes the change legible after reload without becoming a noisy activity feed.

findings.observation: The current language is precise for a trust-sensitive workflow, but source authorization and relationship memory may still sound technical to a recruiter who thinks in terms of notes and conversations.
findings.evidence: Browser replay shows source authorization, governed source, and relationship memory in the confirmation layer.
findings.user_impact: The decision is safe, while first-time comprehension may be slower than necessary.
findings.recommendation: Field-test a shorter title such as Stop using this source while retaining the precise consequence summary underneath.
findings.verification: Five independent recruiters can accurately explain revoke versus delete and revoke versus restore after one read.

findings.observation: The slice removes a real trust and recovery risk, but no working recruiter has yet compared it with deleting notes, editing an ATS, or manually remembering what to ignore.
findings.evidence: All runtime and browser evidence is local and synthetic.
findings.user_impact: Operational integrity is proven; frequency, willingness to pay, and perceived value remain unknown.
findings.recommendation: Run consented field replays where a recruiter withdraws one source after it affected preparation, then measure correction time, trust, and repeat use.
findings.verification: Compare baseline and Talent Signal across at least five permission-change events per recruiter.

missing_evidence: Team handoff when the decision maker and source owner differ.

reviews.lens: authorization, provenance, derived-state integrity, privacy, and reversibility
strengths: Raw-source retention and evidence authorization are represented as separate lifecycles.
The compiler, resource detail, claim decision, evidence review, proposal, and research entry points all enforce current authorization.
Revocation preserves only audit-safe metadata while hiding locator, fragments, claim proposals, and evidence counts.
Confirmed state is retracted, surviving prior state can become contested, and dependent actions and approvals are revoked.
Restore returns fragments and claims to review and never restores confirmed state, approvals, or actions.
Legacy message-backed and exact fragment-backed claims follow the same retraction contract.
Optimistic versions, idempotency, active-effect reconciliation, snapshot invalidation, and manifest invalidation are explicit.
Executing or unknown actions block revocation until reconciliation rather than pretending the external effect can be undone.

findings.observation: Manual revoke and restore are executable, but the authorization state has no independent expiry timestamp or scheduled transition.
findings.evidence: The migration stores authorization state, reason, and changed time; runtime proof covers manual decisions only.
findings.user_impact: Purpose withdrawal is safe when recorded, while time-bounded permission still depends on a future explicit decision.
findings.recommendation: Add an authorization-expiry clock only when the product has a defensible source of that deadline; route expiry through the same transaction, audit, invalidation, and recompilation contract.
findings.verification: At expiry, evidence becomes unavailable, dependent state and actions retract, Wiki and Chat rebuild, and restore still requires review.

findings.observation: The runtime proves approved but unexecuted action revocation. Completed effects are counted for recruiter follow-up but cannot be undone by this source-memory transition.
findings.evidence: The response exposes completed_actions_requiring_follow_up; the replay count was zero.
findings.user_impact: The system does not overclaim reversibility, but the Web confirmation does not yet demonstrate the completed-effect warning state.
findings.recommendation: Add a synthetic completed-effect fixture and surface an explicit follow-up warning when the count is nonzero.
findings.verification: Revocation preserves the observed outcome, removes future authority, and shows the recruiter what external follow-up may still be needed.

missing_evidence: Production retention policy for free-text authorization rationale.

adjudication.resolved_prior_finding: Permission-change recovery now retracts unauthorized content and derivatives, recompiles Wiki and Chat context from surviving sources, and exposes only audit-safe Agent history.
adjudication.release_boundary: This result does not pass the full multichannel product or production release. Automatic authorization expiry, completed-effect follow-up, cross-account runtime denial, field comparison, and commercial evidence remain open.
adjudication.next_highest_risk_test: Exercise an authorization deadline and one already completed observed effect through the same invalidation and recruiter-warning path.
